agent: W2-10 gap critic: user and developer experience
summary: Gap critique of user and developer experience: seven findings, five reproduced at user level, and one production defect outside PAR 4. In D.2's favour: type-error text comes from the imperative checker after the on-network fallback, so it does not depend on which contradiction the network recorded (this narrows C5-8), and §7's canonical round records would repair today's VS Code round view, which is wrong in three ways. (1) An exception in a fire hangs the run silently: today on rounds of 8 or more under the production thread executor, and at every width under a persistent executor (P3's shape), which also writes into its creation-time stdout, the LSP's JSON-RPC stream. (2) D.2 routes system faults (late writes, 158, fuel exhaustion, C6-4's exceptions) through the program's contradiction channel, whose consumers absorb or misreport them: `:fuel 1` reports a correct process as a 'protocol violation', `:timeout 0` returns answers silently, and typing never reads the network contradiction, so 'late-s0-write is not the inductive evidence §14 claims. (3) Nothing in D.2 owns the user knobs (`:timeout`, `:fuel`, `:execution`, `:parallelism`, `:fairness`), and an inline solver override silently resets every other key, a production defect that turns a working well-founded query into a crash that aborts the whole file. (4) '2 seeds' cannot name an OS-thread interleaving, printed answers already differ between identical sequential runs (the order of gensym consumption varies), and the replay reproduces the canonical answer rather than the failing run; a seeded simulated-K executor plus a read-version log is proposed. (5–7) The LSP needs round records after the fact rather than O-11's request at S0 entry; the E1006 derivation is computed inside an S0 fire from reads of the whole network; and P3's gate needs a dispersion row, against today's CV of 0.03–0.05 with the executor on or off.

findings.lens: R (reality check) / developer and editor experience
findings.section: D.2 §6.7 (Executors; Contradiction), §10.2 (no row for a raising fire), §14 P3; production executor driver.rkt:567; C6-4, CL-13
findings.claim_attacked: §6.7 'Executors: persistent OS-level threads … created once per process, parked between solves' and 'Contradiction: ⊤ in the contradiction cell; executors see it at their next lane check and stop'. D.2 has no path for a fire that raises.
findings.severity: major (a blocker for P3 as written; a latent production defect today)
findings.evidence:
MEASUREMENT, exec-exn.rkt. One round of N propagators over one source cell; one fire raises.
- sequential-fire-all: raises 'fire: internal fault in propagator k' at N=4 and at N=12.
- Production thread-per-round executor: at N=4 (below its threshold of 8) it raises. At N=12 it HANGS, and the exception text goes to the run's error port.
- Persistent worker (created before the run, P3's shape): HANGS at N=4 and at N=12. Its text goes to the process stderr captured at creation (exec-exn.err), not to the run's port.
- Power rows: with no raising fire, all six legs return ok.

Mechanism:
- propagator.rkt:3715-3727: `thread #:pool 'own` calls `channel-put` only on success, the joiner blocks in `channel-get`, and there is no handler. fire-propagator (:377-379) has no handler either.
- The LSP sends both error and output ports to nowhere (lsp/server.rkt:543-545). It is synchronous, and `$/cancelRequest` is a no-op (:453). A hang therefore wedges the server with an empty log.

exec-port.rkt: the caller sets current-output-port to nowhere, as server.rkt:545 does ('stdout IS the LSP JSON-RPC channel'). A fire that displays 'LEAK' still writes 4 bytes into the protocol stream under the persistent worker. Sequential and thread-per-round write 0.

Reach:
- Merges run inside fires and call whnf (type-lattice.rkt:300-301, 403-404). whnf raises `error 'reduction "fuel exhausted"` (reduction.rkt:2861).
- User `net-add-prop` fires run whnf (reduction.rkt:4440).
- The debug invariant checks in fire-and-collect-writes (:2951-2964, current-check-fire-invariants?; the comment says 'caught LOUDLY') would hang instead of reporting, on rounds of 8 or more.

Not shown at user level: u5's divergent type-level function raises on the main thread (process-command/demand), so it aborts the whole file but does not hang (u5-type-fuel.out).
findings.direction:
Exceptions become data at the scheduler layer.
- The fire wrapper that every scheduler shares (C2-6/CL-13) catches exn:fail per fire. It appends (propagator id, srcloc, exn, epoch) to a per-executor fault lane, and the faults join into a monotone fault-set cell.
- The detector treats a non-empty fault set as a stop condition, as it treats contradiction. In-flight deltas are counted as consumed and discarded, so the counters balance (C5-8).
- The boundary re-raises one fault, chosen in canonical order (smallest propagator id, or derivation depth from the replay), on the caller's thread. That is the exception the sequential run raises, so the user-visible outcome is the same at every K and every width.
- The same wrapper installs the run's ports from the run record, never the executor's creation-time ones. The P1b ban on IO in S0 stays.
- New semantic axis S-11, 'a fire raises': identical user-visible error at K ∈ {1,4,8,16}, at both widths, and under the LSP's port redirection. exec-exn.rkt's N=12 leg is its power row.
- Apply the wrapper to today's executor in P0.5, unless O-14 deletes that executor first (CL-2).
findings.falsifier: A census showing that no S0 fire body and no installed merge can raise (no reachable whnf, `error` or `raise`). Or a documented Racket guarantee that an exception in a parallel thread propagates to the thread that joins it.
findings.confidence: high for the mechanism; medium for production reach

findings.section: D.2 §6.1 (158: 'an error (a classified contradiction)'), §6.7 'Late writes', §8, §10.2 S-4/S-6/S-10, §14 P3 inductive column; C6-4's direction; CL-9, CL-10
findings.claim_attacked: §14 P3, inductive column: "'late-s0-write makes a detection bug a contradiction". S-6: "'tropical-fuel-exhausted under every schedule". The common assumption that a classified contradiction is a visible, distinguishable outcome.
findings.evidence:
Three production consumers of a contradiction raised for a reason outside the program.

(a) Session runtime (u9-spawn-fuel). A correct `defproc sender : S` with `strategy tiny :fuel 1` prints 'ERROR: sender process execution failed: protocol violation ([!Nat . end])'. With `:fuel 100000` it prints 'Protocol completed'.
- Mechanism: rt-execute-process maps any contradiction to 'contradiction (session-runtime.rkt:1077-1079), and driver.rkt:1340-1344 renders that as a protocol violation.
- The only test is test-session-runtime-04.rkt:104-112, which accepts 'ok or contradiction', so it pins nothing.

(b) Solver (u3, u4). `solver atms-t0 :strategy atms :timeout 0` gives fuel 0 (relations.rkt:3115-3116).
- The observer recorded exactly one contradicted BSP run per fuel-0 query: 2/2 in u3 and 3/3 in u4. The atms-s control queries recorded 0.
- Every fuel-0 query returned its full answer set with no message.
- dissolve-solver-pu (relations.rkt:2869-) never reads the contradiction. Inside a branch, a contradiction becomes a nogood, i.e. silently fewer answers.

(c) Typing. infer-on-network/full (typing-propagators.rkt:3009-3082) and /err (:3154-3236) never read the network's contradiction.
- Count: 0 occurrences of net-contradiction? or prop-network-contradiction in the file. Power: the same pattern finds relations.rkt:461 and elaborator-network.rkt:254.
- A ⊤ root falls back to the imperative checker (:3198-3200), and a fault elsewhere in the network is simply not read.

Consequences:
- A 'late-s0-write on the elaboration path is invisible to the user and to the suite.
- If anything surfaced the reason symbols, a newcomer would meet scheduler vocabulary ('late-s0-write, 'tropical-fuel-exhausted).
findings.direction:
Separate three outcomes by information flow.
- (1) Program contradiction: ⊤ in a domain lattice. This is the user's error or a logical failure, as today.
- (2) System fault: a scheduler-layer monotone set of (reason, propagator, epoch). Reasons: a late write, structure created in a fire (158), an executor exception (W2-10-1), a fenced cell that oscillates until its budget runs out.
  - It is never written into any cell that a consumer reads as logical failure.
  - The boundary turns it into one diagnostic class: 'internal error in the propagator scheduler — please report', plus the reproduction bundle of W2-10-4. The text names no scheduler concept; K, epochs and fences appear only inside the bundle.
  - The test harness fails any run whose fault set is not empty: a census trap per reason, each with a power row. Only then is §14's inductive claim true.
- (3) User budget exhausted (`:fuel`, `:timeout`, typing's internal budget): a user-facing outcome, 'budget exhausted — results may be incomplete'. It is never 'protocol violation' and never silent. Typing's internal budget stays a silent fallback, but is counted.
findings.falsifier: A consumer census showing that every reader of contradiction distinguishes the reason (none of the three above does). Or an owner decision that budget exhaustion is meant to read as program failure.

findings.lens: U (user-visible semantics) / P (Progressive Disclosure; the monotone-migration rule)
findings.section: D.2 §1 (scope), §6.6 fuel row, §6.7 (K as scheduler-k), §12.2 P6 (the drain deleted), §15 (no O-n for the surface); C2-9, C2-7
findings.claim_attacked: §6.6 'fuel counts changes'; §6.7 'K is scheduler-k, a cell …, default max(1, physical cores − 2)'; P6 deletes the drain. D.2 says nothing about what the surface knobs mean before, during or after the change.
findings.severity: major (one part is a production defect, independent of PAR 4)
findings.evidence:
Measured at user level, one file per process.

(1) `:timeout` is documented in milliseconds (docs/spec/grammar.org:1427 `:timeout 5000`; LOGIC_ENGINE_DESIGN.org:1728-1738). It is implemented as fuel = ms × 1000 fires (relations.rkt:3115-3116). `:timeout 0` still returns the full answers (u3, u4).

(2) An inline override resets every key it does not name.
- Mechanism: elaborator.rkt:3128 builds the override with make-solver-config, which fills in every default (solver.rkt:73-100). reduction.rkt:4675-4690 then merges all of those keys over the named solver.
- u3: `solve-with atms-s {:timeout 0} (two ?x)` gives `@[]` (DFS), while `solve-with atms-s (two ?x)` gives `@[{:x 2}]` (ATMS, PD-1). For `pick`, the answer order is 1..6 with the override and 6..1 without.
- u8: `solve-with wf-solver (p-holds)` gives `@[]`. `solve-with wf-solver {:timeout 100} (p-holds)` aborts the whole file with 'solve: Depth limit exceeded (100)': stratified DFS on cyclic negation, uncaught, and every result in the file is lost. `{:semantics well-founded :timeout 100}` gives `@[]`.
- The repo's own example row, examples/2026-03-14-wfle-acceptance.prologos:642 ('I6: WF with timeout override … accepted via solver config merge'), therefore runs stratified semantics. The bug is masked there because the answers happen to coincide.
- Not filed: docs/tracking mentions solver-config-merge only in design documents.

(3) `:execution :parallel` (the default, solver.rkt:75) selects BSP, and `:sequential` selects the drain (stratified-eval.rkt:299-304), which P6 deletes. On u2's three query pairs the two give identical answers. That is weak evidence: the drain leg in W2-10-6 shows the drain changing a diagnostic.

(4) The strategy keys `:parallelism :single-thread|:work-stealing`, `:fairness` and `:scheduler-io` are validated (macros.rkt:1017-1028) and never read; only `:fuel` is (driver.rkt:1332). Yet the acceptance file declares `:fairness :priority` and `:scheduler-io :blocking-ok` (examples/2026-03-18-track7-acceptance.prologos:161-168), and D.2 §13 rejects work-stealing.
findings.direction:
Give D.2 a surface-contract section and an owner decision.
- (a) K is never a meaning. `:execution` becomes a request for scheduler-k, i.e. data.
  - Under H, every value gives the same answers.
  - For fenced cells, the result is defined by the canonical order (the BSP replay) and K is ignored.
  - Whatever the drain's own semantics carried retires behind a refusal.
- (b) `:timeout` either becomes wall-clock, nondeterministic by nature and reported as 'timed out — results may be incomplete', or it is renamed to a budget with stated units. `:fuel` either keeps fire semantics, or counting changes is recorded as a language change (C2-9). Either way its exhaustion is outcome (3) of W2-10-2.
- (c) `:parallelism`, `:fairness` and `:scheduler-io` become refusals now, under the monotone-migration rule (a refusal keeps every later meaning open), or are mapped onto scheduler data such as the ready queue's priority by kind (CL-14, row 6).
- (d) Fix the merge: an override carries only the user's keys, i.e. elaborator.rkt:3128 builds a raw option map, not a make-solver-config. File it in DEFERRED with u3 and u8 as the reproduction. A per-command conversion of the uncaught 'Depth limit exceeded' would be a separate entry.
findings.falsifier: For (a)–(c): an owner decision placing the solver and strategy knobs in another track, named. For (d): a test showing that `solve-with named {k v}` keeps the other keys of `named`; u3 and u8 currently show it does not.

findings.lens: R (reproducibility) / T (theory of testing concurrent schedulers)
findings.section: D.2 §6.7 Gate ('parity suite at K ∈ {1, 4, 8, 16} × 2 seeds'), §10.2, §6.6 replay monitor, §7 ('the execution view is reserved'), §10.1 RM-2
findings.claim_attacked: That '× 2 seeds' makes K > 1 failures reproducible. That the BSP replay and the reserved execution view cover P3's debugging needs.
findings.evidence:
(i) In test-arena-parity.rkt:75-116, the seed permutes installation order, i.e. a deterministic schedule. At K > 1 the interleaving of OS threads is not a function of any seed, so a failing (K, seed) pair cannot be run again to the same execution.

(ii) gensym-probe2.out: 12 identical runs of atms-adversarial (prod/seq × observer on/off × 3).
- They print 6 distinct pairs of fresh-variable names, e.g. under seq 'b_g2428 … c_g2471' in one run and 'b_g2425 … c_g2470' in another.
- The gensym total is constant (g2565 at the end of all 12 runs), and the three occurrences of c within one answer always agree.
- So what varies between runs is the ORDER in which gensyms are consumed, at K = 1 and independent of the executor.
- Source: relations.rkt:1532/1924, `(format "~a_~a" name (gensym))`.
- Consequences: user-visible output is not byte-reproducible today, and any parity or replay comparison by equal? on values that hold minted names reports false differences.

(iii) The replay re-runs the epoch under BSP from x⁰ₑ (§6.6). It reproduces the canonical result, not the failing interleaving, so a K > 1 bug that the monitor flags cannot be debugged from the replay.
findings.direction:
(a) A deterministic simulated-K executor. K logical executors are multiplexed on one OS thread and run the real lane, ownership and detector code. A seeded scheduler chooses which executor steps and when each lane delivers.
- Seeds then name executions, and the parity rows run here. Use PCT-style priority schedules for coverage: Burckhardt et al., ASPLOS 2010, find a bug of depth d with probability ≥ 1/(n·k^(d−1)).
- PRECEDENT: CHESS (Musuvathi & Qadeer), FoundationDB's simulation testing, Loom.
- The real parallel run becomes the stress tier.

(b) In the real run, record for each fire the epoch-local version (change count) of every input it read.
- With monotone fires and join merges, (x⁰ₑ, read-version log) determines every fire's output, so the failing epoch replays deterministically.
- Dump both on any fault or monitor disagreement.
- This makes RM-2 (materialising x⁰ₑ at K > 1) a reproducibility requirement, not an observation option.
- ESTIMATE: one integer per input per fire.

(c) Make fresh names a function of structural position (clause id × call path × occurrence), or α-normalise them at the boundary. Parity and replay then compare modulo α.

(d) The runner's failure log records K, the seed and the path of the bundle.
findings.falsifier: A demonstration that the parity seeds control the interleaving at K > 1, or that no value written in S0 or printed to the user contains a minted name.
findings.confidence: high for (i)–(iii); the cost of record and replay is an ESTIMATE

findings.section: D.2 §7 (round records 'on request'; O-11), §10.1 RM-1, §12.2 P6 (the current-bsp-observer callback is deleted), §15 O-11; C2-7, C8-11
findings.claim_attacked: §7: 'Round records are the Kleene iterates, on request. Under DIRECT they come from the replay.' O-11's lean (a): 'a parameter read once, by the scheduler, at S0-run entry'. RM-1 is measured 'on the suite'.
findings.evidence:
How the LSP uses rounds:
- It installs the observer on EVERY diagnostics elaboration (lsp/server.rkt:519, 547). At save time it cannot know whether the user will open the view.
- make-trace-accumulator re-stamps round numbers across all runs into one timeline (propagator.rkt:594-604).
- The trace's initial network is the final one (server.rkt:586: 'initial = final for now').

How the view uses them:
- It resets each cell to those 'initial' (final) values and applies each diff's newValue by cellId (propagatorView.ts:1604, 1626-1650).
- newValue is the WRITTEN value, not the merged one: cell-diff is built from `(cdr w)` at propagator.rkt:3568-3571.
- Each diff carries one sourcePropagator (propagatorView.ts:40).

Measured with run-leg.rkt in the LSP's mode (#:evaluate? #f):
- constraints-adversarial: 212 BSP rounds from 66 separate runs;
- type-adversarial: 182 rounds from 61 runs.
The view shows each as one history of one network.

Under P2 with lean (a), the LSP has to request rounds on every save, which means a BSP replay of every epoch per save. ESTIMATE: one extra BSP S0 per epoch, against S0 being 24–30 % of the work (P0 §0). RM-1 is not measured on that path.
findings.direction:
Name the consumers and add an option to O-11.
- §7 lists the LSP, the observatory and the VS Code view as consumers (C2-7).
- O-11 gains option (c), a post-hoc query:
  - Epoch records retain x⁰ₑ for the last elaboration of each open document: a pointer at K = 1, materialised at K > 1 (RM-2).
  - When the user selects a (network, epoch), the view asks over LSP for that epoch's rounds.
  - The save path pays only for epoch records.
- State the change to the wire format: network and epoch keys, old and held values, a set of writers in place of sourcePropagator, and a schema version.
- State the gain, which is in D.2's favour. Round records are the Kleene iterates, so the scrubber becomes scheduler-independent, and it becomes correct where today it is not (initial = final, written ≠ held, runs conflated). Land this in P2 together with a test of the view.
findings.falsifier: An owner decision deprecating the round view, or RM-1 measured on the LSP's save path at ≤ 1.1×.

findings.section: D.2 §7 (derivations over rounds), §1 (out of scope: error explanation on rounds, DEFERRED 176 (c), (d)), §6.3 row 8 and the fence, §10.2 (no row for diagnostic parity); C5-8, C9-7, C2-12 (cell-19)
findings.claim_attacked: §1 places error explanation on rounds out of scope, while the production explanation is computed inside an S0 fire. C5-8 asks, as its falsifier, whether any consumer reads which cell was contradicted.
findings.evidence:
(a) This narrows C5-8, in D.2's favour.
- Type-error text comes from the imperative checker after the on-network fallback (typing-propagators.rkt:3194-3225; driver.rkt:774, 850, 977, 1910), so it does not depend on which contradiction the network recorded.
- The contradicted cell's identity reaches message text only through:
  - extract-contradiction-info (elaborator-network.rkt:259-267), whose caller elab-solve has no production caller;
  - the session checks (session-propagators.rkt:618, session-type-bridge.rkt:388), whose only callers are tests;
  - the trace view (trace-serialize.rkt:164).
- A/B over 7 corpus files (ab/; eval mode; one process per run; production executor vs sequential): 0 differing result lines, except the gensym names in atms-adversarial, which also vary between runs of the same leg (W2-10-4).
- Power row, same instrument with the drain leg: type-adversarial.prologos:85 (`[map … [map … xs]]`) prints `'[4 6 8 10 12]` under BSP. Under the drain (2/2 runs) it prints 'No instance of Buildable for List … Available instances: … Buildable List …', a message that contradicts itself.

(b) The `because:` lines of the user-facing E1006 come from cell-19. An S0 fire writes it (typing-propagators.rkt:1379-1421) by calling static-reverse-walk (error-explanation.rkt:181-205).
- The walk reads every propagator and the raw values of the cells it visits, and it reads current-command-atms (error-explanation.rkt:261). Those reads lie far outside the fire's declared input, cell-18. The first chain emitted wins (:1399).
- BSP walks a round snapshot. DIRECT at K = 1 walks the live network: deterministic, but possibly a different text. The `because:` lines are pinned in tests/test-elaboration-parity.rkt and test-provenance-errors.rkt. At K > 1 the walk reads other executors' slots mid-epoch, so the text is nondeterministic.
- Reach not measured: u7 reached only the imperative E1006 path (1 BSP run).

(c) Whether a command takes the on-network type or falls back depends on order wherever a merge is not a join (F3(b), §6.3 row 8). At K > 1 a leak in the fence (CL-4 (c), S-9 fails) therefore shows up as an error that appears and disappears between saves.
findings.direction:
In-fire diagnostics write only monotone facts: the position and the contradicted aids (cell-18 already is such a fact). The derivation is computed at the boundary, from the quiescent state or from the epoch's round records. That is §7's derivation, and it moves into P2's scope because a production consumer exists.

Add S-12: a file with two independent type errors, two union exhaustions and a solver contradiction gives byte-identical diagnostics (after α-normalisation) at K ∈ {1,4,8,16}, under the simulated-K seeds, and under the replay. Power row: the drain leg above.
findings.falsifier: A measurement showing that the in-fire E1006 path is unreachable in production, which reduces (b) to dead code to delete. And S-9 holding under the chosen fence, which removes (c).

findings.section: D.2 §6.7 (Gate; the default for K), §14 P3, performance column; C6-5, C7-3
findings.claim_attacked: P3's gate reports speedup only. 'default max(1, physical cores − 2)'.
findings.evidence:
MEASUREMENT, variance.rkt, run under the suite lock: 15 interleaved repetitions per leg, load 3.5–4.1 on 18 cores (uptime recorded in the output).

| file | executor | wall median (min–max) | CV |
|---|---|---|---|
| constraints-adversarial | production | 67 ms (63–75) | 0.049 |
| constraints-adversarial | sequential | 44 ms (42–49) | 0.040 |
| type-adversarial | production | 59 ms (58–62) | 0.027 |
| type-adversarial | sequential | 38 ms (37–42) | 0.038 |

- Today's thread executor costs about 1.5× but adds no dispersion. Today's run-to-run spread (CV ≈ 0.03–0.05) is therefore the bar a K > 1 design must hold.
- 'cores − 2' per process ignores co-tenants: the runner's ~18 workers (C6-5), an LSP that elaborates on every save, and a REPL.
findings.direction:
- Add a dispersion row to the P3 gate: CV and p90/median at a stated load, on the heavy files and the medium tier.
- Add an oversubscription row: runner workers × K > cores, and an LSP running alongside a suite run.
- Inside the test runner and the LSP, K defaults to 1 until a measurement says otherwise (C7-3).
- A machine-level budget grants K; the suite lock already arbitrates machine-wide. Neither a newcomer nor a test author ever sets K.
findings.falsifier: P3 measurements whose CV stays within today's baseline under oversubscription.
